correctness.rationale: Exact rook expansion and group stabilizer argument prove uniform orbit divisibility for all \(k\ge1\). Legendre valuation and digit-sum bound make every nonconstant term vanish modulo \(2^n\). Since \(\nu_2(n!)=n-1\), all permanents are odd multiples of \(2^{n-1}\); Fourier/invertibility conclusions follow. Replayed integer subset-DP checker covers 142 sign-pattern cases but is not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The congruence determines a natural exact \(2\)-adic invariant uniformly across exponentially many signed matching weights, yielding a strong noncancellation theorem for a natural cyclic matching Fourier quotient. It gives invertibility and a quantitative inverse bound despite explicit zeros in the unrestricted full matching Fourier operator. The proof is an infinite-family structural orbit result, not a finite computation or generic normalization check; unresolved older congruence coverage is separately acknowledged.
